dedupe_keys.name: senegal temporary migration estimates from mobile phones

description: This Senegal dataset publishes temporary migration estimates derived from mobile-phone observations for 2013–2015. The Blanchard and Rubrichi research team provides origin-destination-time statistics across 39 cities and 112 rural areas defined using third-level administrative units. Estimates are resolved to half-month periods. The Figshare deposit contains compressed CSV tables with weighted and unweighted variants, sample definitions and minimum-duration thresholds identified in filenames. It is freely available under CC BY 4.0. Companion Python and R scripts document how daily locations, home locations, migration segments and observation gaps are inferred before aggregation and weighting. These tables can inform changing population demand, transport-flow scenarios and agent-based models such as model-matsim. They describe estimated temporary migration, not direct counts of all residents or all trips. Phone ownership, observation gaps, home-location rules and weighting assumptions affect interpretation. The released spatial and temporal aggregation also limits applications requiring street-level routes or daily travel timing. No underlying individual call records were retrieved during this metadata review.
